GLASS HOUSE HEIST — REBUILD · PHASE 1

UI DIRECTION

Research first: how the best game interfaces in the industry earn their place — then five style directions for our game, same composition each time so only the style differs. Pick one below.

01 — HOW THE BEST DO IT

Reference screens from the industry canon (full analysis in ui-research.md). The lessons we carry forward: diegetic state, contextual HUD, feedback on every input, consistency as brand, quiet-when-idle.

02 — PICK A STYLE DIRECTION

All five mockups show the same screen (menu + HUD strip + mascot + gameplay glimpse) so you're comparing style only. Note: the AI invented different game titles per style — ignore names, judge the design language.

HOW TO CHOOSE

  1. B (hologram) maps 1:1 to the heist fiction — encryption, validators and the vault all become UI.
  2. A (flat neon) is the safest premium choice and best matches the hi-res mascot art as-is.
  3. D (Swiss) is the boldest, least-"AI" option — one color decision and typographic confidence.
  4. C (speedrun) is the loudest — likely the right identity for Glass Dash rather than the heist.
  5. E (pixel) looks great but forces a pixel-art commitment across every asset (biggest cascade).

Hybrid is possible later (e.g. A for the game + C for Dash), but the rebuild starts with one primary direction.

Sources: Interface.InGame · Game UI Database · StringLabs UI case studies · SunStrike "What is Game UI" · Game Design Skills · platformer HUD pattern research — full citations in ui-research.md.
